sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the three aspects of upper and lower union, attaining the completion of receiving the Torah requires not only self-nullification but also the full existence of soul and body connected to the Torah, as exemplified by Mordechai's Torah study which aroused Israel to study with mesirus nefesh, drawing down the elevation of Torah study from the perspective of human perfection.

translations.translation: a)
And now, based on what was explained above
(section 4)
that in the union of upper and lower there are three matters – the upper,
the lower, and their nullification – it is understood
that in order to merit the completion and perfection of receiving the Torah, the nullification of the soul and the body is not sufficient;
rather, their existence must also be present,
and as they are in their ultimate perfection,
and that their existence be connected and joined with the Torah.
And in the manner explained above
(sections 6 and 8)
that the advantage of Torah study for its own sake is not only in the matter of nullification
(that his study is not for the sake of his own perfection,
nor even for the perfection of the soul)
but also that the existence of the person studying
(the soul and the body)
becomes connected with the Torah, through which he emerges from his limitations and rises to the boundlessness of Torah.
And it may be said
that this is what is brought in the maamar – that the arousal of mesirus nefesh of Israel was through Mordechai,
Moshe of his generation,
for Mordechai's Torah study was in the ultimate elevation,
and by arousing Israel to study Torah with mesirus nefesh
[and particularly since Mordechai was the head of the generation
(like Moshe)
from whom it is drawn to all the limbs],
he drew into them
(not only the matter of nullification,
but)
also the elevation of Torah study as it is from the perspective of the perfection of the person,
the perfection of the soul and the body.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains why Mordechai gathered twenty-two thousand schoolchildren, for the advantage of Torah study from the perfection of soul and body is primarily in schoolchildren, whose breath sustains the world because their souls are closer to G-dliness and their bodies less materialized, and through Mordechai this elevation was drawn to all Jews of that generation.

translations.translation: And based on this, we may also explain what is brought in the maamar that Mordechai gathered twenty-two thousand schoolchildren,
for this advantage in Torah study
(which is from the perspective of the perfection of the soul and the body)
is primarily in schoolchildren.
And this will be understood based on what our sages said,
"The world endures only for the sake of the breath of schoolchildren."
Rav Pappa said to Abaye, "What about mine and yours?"
He said to him, "The breath that has sin is not like the breath that has no sin."
For although the Torah study of Rav Pappa and Abaye was
(certainly)
for its own sake in the most exalted levels, and the Torah study of schoolchildren is from fear of the strap,
nevertheless,
there is an advantage in the breath of schoolchildren,
for specifically on this breath the world endures.
And the explanation of this is known,
that the advantage in the breath of schoolchildren is both from the perspective of their souls,
which are closer to G-dliness because they have recently come from the spiritual world,
and from the perspective of their bodies, which have not become so materialized in coarse desires and lusts,
as explained elsewhere at length.
And based on this, it may be said
that this which is brought in the maamar – that at the time of the decree Mordechai gathered twenty-two thousand schoolchildren –
is
in order to explain that in the Torah study that took place then,
there was
(not only the nullification of the soul and the body,
but)
also the perfection of the soul and the body.
[However, the advantage of the soul of schoolchildren is not relevant
(so much)
to their Torah study,
since their study is from fear of the strap
(the nature of the body)
and not from the soul,
and there is also no nullification of mesirus nefesh in it;
therefore the maamar brings that the study of schoolchildren was through Mordechai,
through which their Torah study was also with mesirus nefesh, as explained in the maamar.]
And it may be added
that by Mordechai gathering twenty-two thousand schoolchildren, there was added to him the elevation of the breath of schoolchildren,
and through this
he drew this matter also to all the Jews of his generation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: On Purim one must become intoxicated until he does not know, because the perfection of receiving the Torah comes through nullification, and this nullification must be from the body as well, thereby drawing strength for the entire year so that bodily matters do not hinder Torah study.

translations.translation: b)
And based on this, we may also explain what is required – that a person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know,
for on the days of Purim, every year, the matter of "the Jews accepted" is reawakened as it was the first time,
and moreover – in a manner of ascending in holiness.
[And it may be added
that the innovation of the days of Purim relative to the giving of the Torah is in two matters.
On the days of Purim there was the completion and perfection of receiving the Torah
("and the Jews accepted"),
as explained above at length,
and also the permanence of the Torah,
as it is stated in the Gemara
on the verse
"The Jews fulfilled and accepted" – they fulfilled what they had already accepted,
for what they received at the giving of the Torah was not in a manner of eternal permanence,
since after they sinned with the calf they removed the ornaments,
and on the days of Purim it is written
"These days of Purim shall not pass... and their memory shall not cease from their seed,"
for what they accepted on Purim endured with eternal permanence.
And likewise on the days of Purim every year,
there are these two matters.
Each year, additional perfection is added to the receiving of the Torah
(as above),
and also this addition has eternal permanence.]
Therefore on Purim there must be the service of "does not know,"
going out of oneself,
for the perfection of receiving the Torah comes through nullification.
And this is also that the departure from one's existence
(until "does not know")
must be through becoming intoxicated with wine
(physical),
for the nullification
(of Purim)
must also be from the perspective of the body,
as explained above at length.
And from this is drawn the empowerment for the entire year,
that bodily matters will not occupy a place for him, and consequently there will be no hindrance from the body to Torah study.
